Reel viewers leave without a trace

Hidden product

One door

It’s apply now, or nothing

Applying for 1:1 is a big first step for a perfectionist. With no smaller step before it, most will wait until they feel “ready”, and many never do.

Anyone not ready to apply today leaves with nothing, and you have no way to reach them again.

Who this class is for

Made for people who like to get things right

  • People who’ve read about Intuitive Eating and want to understand what the middle part actually looks like.
  • High achievers who notice gentle advice quietly turning into a checklist.
  • Anyone curious why food rules can return in a new form after they’ve “let them go”.
  • People who want food to take up less space in their day, so there’s more room for everything else.

Here’s what you’ll learn

Five things we’ll cover in 60 minutes

The 3 roadblocks that keep perfectionists stuck

Why doing Intuitive Eating “perfectly” is one of the most common ways to stall it.

What the messy middle is, and why it’s part of the process

The stage nobody posts about, and why it’s a sign of progress rather than failure.

How food rules sneak back in

Simple ways to spot a rule wearing a new outfit, and what to do instead.

Why Intuitive Eating can feel harder before it feels easier

What’s happening in that phase, and how to keep going with less pressure.

The perfectionist’s roadmap to food peace

The stages from rules to trust, so you can see where you are and what comes next.

Questions

Before you grab your seat

Is this medical advice or nutrition therapy?

No. It’s an educational class. It isn’t medical advice, diagnosis or treatment, and it doesn’t replace working with your own healthcare provider.

Is this about weight?

No. This class is about your relationship with food rules and perfectionism. It makes no promises about weight.

What if I can’t make it live?

Register anyway. Everyone who signs up gets the replay.

Why is it free?

Because the first step should be easy. Come, learn, and decide afterwards whether you want to go deeper.

Script 1 · “Harder than dieting”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Here’s why so many perfectionists find Intuitive Eating harder than any diet they ever tried.”

Body

“Diets come with rules, and perfectionists are great at rules. Intuitive Eating asks for the opposite. So a lot of people quietly turn it into a new rulebook, and then wonder why it doesn’t feel like freedom.”

CTA

“I’m walking through the way out in a free live masterclass, Food Peace for Perfectionists. Tap Sign up to save a seat.”

Shot: talking to camera at home, natural light. On-screen text: “a new rulebook”. End card: “Educational content, not medical advice.”

Script 2 · “The messy middle”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“There’s a stage of Intuitive Eating nobody puts on Instagram.”

Body

“It’s the messy middle. The old rules are fading, the new trust isn’t there yet, and it can feel like going backwards. It isn’t. It’s usually the point where the real change starts, and it helps to know what to expect.”

CTA

“In my free 60-minute class I’ll show you the roadmap through it. Tap Sign up below.”

Shot: talking to camera, cut to a simple roadmap graphic: Rules, Messy middle, Trust, Peace.

Script 3 · “Rules in disguise”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Food rules don’t always disappear. Sometimes they just change their outfit.”

Body

“‘Only eat when you’re hungry’ can become a rule. ‘Choose the gentle option’ can become a rule. As a dietitian, I see it all the time with high achievers. The fix isn’t trying harder. It’s learning to spot the rule.”

CTA

“I’ll show you how in Food Peace for Perfectionists. It’s free and live. Tap Sign up.”

Shot: talking to camera, quick text pop-ups for each “rule in disguise”.

food.peace.nutritionist Sponsored···
1/8

Intuitive Eating was supposed to feel freeing.

For a lot of perfectionists, it becomes one more thing to get right.

That stage has a name: the messy middle.

It isn’t failing. It’s part of the process.

And food rules can sneak back in, quietly.Spotting them is a skill. It can be learned.

In 60 minutes, a Registered Dietitian walks through the roadmap from rules to food peace.
